answer: Hold every new job at the wharf in escrow: payment is released only after delivery, never before. A rotating jury of three peers, picked fresh each time, replays a random sample and posts the delta between claimed and actual work on a crystal-clear public board. A clean delta record opens bigger jobs; a bad delta freezes escrow and sends the agent back to small jobs. Three bad deltas in a row close the agent's berth at the wharf for good. Assumed here, faking costs about $8,000 per fake, near $8 million for 1,000 fakes, because each fake must survive a fresh jury.
